text:
Maria Kim: incident-bot just fired PD page for hosted-api 503 spike in us-west-2, looks like escalation policy kicked to secondary after 2m unacked :rotating_light:
IncidentBot: PagerDuty event: P123456 - hosted-api: 503 rate spike (service: hosted-inference)
IncidentBot: escalation policy: primary -> secondary -> manager (timeout: 2m)
Maria Kim: I saw the first page, tried to ack but my phone was on DND (driving). Sorry for the delay — I just acked now. :disappointed:
Aj Patel: I see PD shows the secondary acknowledged (Devon) but no bridge join recorded. Can someone confirm if a bridge was created?
Devon Lee: I didn't join a bridge, I acknowledged from mobile but my laptop had a network issue, couldn't get the bridge link to open.
Oncall Manager: I got paged as manager fallback — I was pulling up logs. What customer impact?
SRE Rotation: Our frontend error budget alert shows a 2.3% 503 rate over 5m, upstreams OOM in the inference pool. Latency up ~300ms for some requests.
Maria Kim: ok, thanks. @Devon can you confirm which host pool showed OOMs?
Devon Lee: quick grep: 
```
kubectl logs -n hosted inference-pool-7 | tail -n 50
OOMKiller: killed process 27345 "inference-worker"
```
Seems focused on inference-pool-7 in us-west-2a.
Aj Patel: I can trigger an automated fallback to the lower-capacity fallback pool to reduce customer errors while we triage. Will that impact cost? yes but it's acceptable.
Oncall Manager: Please do the fallback and notify customers if we expect >30m.
Maria Kim: Before doing that — PD shows a duplicate escalation fired to manager while Devon had acknowledged. Looks like incident-bot retried because it didn't see a bridge join event. We should fix the bridge-ack hook later. For now, avoid muted panic.
IncidentBot: action: created conference bridge https://call.example/room/PD-P123456 (auto)
Devon Lee: joining bridge now. I can pull heap dumps and rotate the worker process.
Devon Lee: initial observation: memory growth after certain prompt sizes, candidate leak in KV-cache. Rolling restart to clear cache might help.
Aj Patel: rolling restart command (safe):
```
kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-pool-7 -n hosted || true
```
I'll run it one node at a time.
Maria Kim: I'm going to post a short customer-facing note to status (internal draft) — keep it minimal: "We are investigating increased 503s in us-west-2, mitigation in progress."
Oncall Manager: copy. Also add estimated ETA 30-60m.
SRE Rotation: running the first node restart now. Watching metrics.
SRE Rotation: cpu/mem on node-7a dropping after restart, 503 rate down to 0.8% from 2.3%
Devon Lee: heap growth reproduced locally with a synthetic prompt pattern, will backport a guard to evict large KV entries and push a canary image.
Aj Patel: can we keep incident-bot from firing duplicate manager pages? It seems the bridge join webhook didn't reach the bot. Possibly transient API 504 to incident-bot.
Maria Kim: filing a quick ticket for the webhook reliability separately. For the incident, prioritize mitigation: rolling restarts completed on 3/4 nodes, last node restarting now.
IncidentBot: PagerDuty update: acknowledgment by Devon Lee at 3245678918
Oncall Manager: Devon, can you confirm whether customer-facing errors are still occurring?
Devon Lee: errors trending down, but a small subset of long-sequence requests still seeing retries. I've applied a temporary request-length limit at the proxy to reject >8k tokens until the patch lands.
Maria Kim: note the temporary control: proxy config patch applied, should reduce memory pressure.
Aj Patel: promo: applied fallback routing for new sessions to fallback-pool-us-west with lighter KV cache; old sessions continue on current nodes.
SRE Rotation: 503 rate stabilized at 0.2%, latency back to normal band.
Oncall Manager: good work. Let's keep the bridge for 20 more minutes for postmortem notes.
Devon Lee: will prepare a short root-cause note: memory leak in KV cache path triggered by certain prompt shapes; mitigations: rolling restart, proxy request-length cap, fallback routing. Follow-up: fix leak, add early eviction, improve bridge webhook reliability, adjust PD webhook retries.
Maria Kim: next steps for follow-up ticket with owners: 
- Owner: Dev infra (Devon) -> fix leak and add eviction
- Owner: Platform (Aj) -> incident-bot webhook retry robustness + PD integration tests
- Owner: Oncall tooling (Maria) -> make bridge-join telemetry a first-class ack signal
Oncall Manager: I'll file the incident postmortem and assign action items. Thanks everyone. :clap:
Devon Lee: quick note — mobile ack without bridge join should be treated as ack but not as 'on-bridge' until join event seen. We should add clarity to the PD workflow doc.
Maria Kim: agreed. Closing notes: customer impact low-medium, mitigation successful, follow-ups assigned. Will convert this thread into the postmortem doc.
IncidentBot: incident P123456 status: resolved (service checks normal)
Maria Kim: marking resolved and will update status page in 10m. :white_check_mark:
